Hi Laila —

Appreciate the clear asks. Summary of our recommended orchestration below; I included internal owners on the CC to validate operational detail.

High-level plan (canary → staged split → full cutover):
1) Preflight (48–24h before window): confirm backups + export KV cache snapshot; validate control-plane HA; upload signed maintenance-agreement (see attachment).
2) Canary (T0): deploy patch to a single canary pod in each AZ, strip nonessential integrations, run smoke tests (5m sampling of 2k requests).
3) Traffic split (T0 + 30m): route 10% traffic to patched canary, 90% to baseline. Monitor 4 KPIs: 99p latency, error rate, token divergence, and CPU/gpu spike.
4) Staged ramp (every 30–60m): 10→25→50→100% with automated abort if any trigger tripped.
5) Pinning & shelve option: we will hold a pinned baseline image on your registry so you can unpin clients in 15m rollback window.
6) Rollback triggers: error rate > 1.5x baseline OR sustained latency regression > 30% for 10m OR failed eviction of KV cache for two consecutive tries.
7) Network drain: graceful connection drain from edge gateways (BGP/peer flap protection), ensure session affinity TTL respected.
8) Postflight (24h): run smoke+eval prompts set, gather audit logs, create AAR.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a 4-hour maintenance window during your low-traffic period (we suggested Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC).
- Control-plane ops will run a small traffic-split script (we provide) that integrates with your netops.
- If we hit an abort, our default is immediate traffic reversion to baseline (no partial pinning) then triage; emergency unpin within 15 minutes.

Please see attached: greenroute_patch_checklist_v1.pdf (draft), network-evacuation-diagram.png.

@Neha / @Soojin / @Karthik / @Dev — can you call out any missing low-level gating (KV drain, cache invalidation, firewall state) or objections to the failure thresholds above?

Thanks,
Maya
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: greenroute_patch_checklist_v1.pdf, network-evacuation-diagram.png

Subject: Re: Private environment patch coordination — implementation detail

Thanks Maya — couple of implementation details from infra:

1) KV cache & state: before canary we will snapshot the embedding KV cache (S3 link) and enable read-only replicas. On rollback we have a utility that replays the last consistent KV state to nodes; full restore ETA ~12m for a pod group of this size.
2) Control-plane: we need to quiesce autoscaler hooks for the patch window (disable scale-ups for T0 — T0+2h) or we risk capacity churn.
3) Network: edge gateways will do BGP graceful drain. For on-prem racks where BGP is not available, NetOps will flip port configs; plan includes a 90s graceful connection TTL before forcing.
4) Firewall & IPS rules: if the patch changes TLS libs, coordinate to accept new cipher suites during the window — otherwise clients may fail TLS handshakes post-cutover.
5) Debugging access: we need mutually agreed read-only SSH jumpbox credentials for the 4-hour window (can be time-limited).

I've attached a shortened ops-runbook that lists exact CLI commands and the KV replay command (greenroute_patch_checklist_v1.pdf). Also added suggested threshold tweaks: set abort error rate to 1.2x baseline for canary; raise to 1.5x for staged ramp.

-Neha
Staff Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: greenroute_patch_checklist_v1.pdf

On Tue, Jul 21, 2026 at 08:15 AM neha_kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> I've attached a shortened ops-runbook that lists exact CLI commands and the KV replay command (greenroute_patch_checklist_v1.pdf).

All good from safety side. Two operational clarifications:
- Pinning lifecycle: we will create a pinned tag on your image registry (greenroute:stable-pin-20260719). The pin will persist for up to 72 hours unless explicitly shelved sooner. Shelving (temporary hold) can be done at any point; emergency unpin requires SOX/Change board approval only if we escalate beyond a single rollback.
- Emergency criteria: add a manual 'shelve' option if partial degradations observed that are recoverable by config toggles (e.g., model quantization flags), so we can avoid a full revert if business impact is low.

I'll add the shelve/unpin decision tree to the checklist and link the runbook here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GRe4n-route-maintenance

—Soojin
